Two render paths: (1) conversion path (src/sars/html_out.py) redraws a specific PDF at recovered coordinates; (2) templated path (src/sars/templates/*) rebuilds a report from extracted data alone.

diagnosis: The user's complaints, grounded in code: (1) FIDELITY - the templated render is too small/narrow and drops per-cell colours because base.TEMPLATE_CSS forces `.report{font-size:6.5pt}` / `.report.compact{font-size:4.6pt;line-height:1.04}` as an inherited fallback (chrome + any un-pooled cell renders too small), and the hand-coded schools_rank._thead/_summary_html structure diverges from the reference PDF's real grouped-header/summary geometry (visible in the compare JPG). (2) ARCHITECTURE - every template funnels through base.document_html which injects a SINGLE shared DOC_CSS+TEMPLATE_CSS and shared chrome across ALL report types; the conversion path writes ONE shared output/html/styles.css linked by every file. The user demands each report be fully self-contained (own structure, own complete inline styling per report type), no shared CSS, no forced common chrome, no cross-report harmonization.
critical_steering_clarification: USER STEERING (authoritative, 'DATA SHOULD BE DATA NOT STYLES'): the extracted data (output/data/*.json + sars.schema dataclasses) must carry ONLY DATA - the figures, names, ranks, counts, GPA, competency labels, structure/grouping - NOT presentation/styles. The prior task (task-template-visual-fidelity FEAT-001, already committed) WRONGLY baked recovered per-cell CellStyle (font family/size/weight/italic/text-colour/background hex) and per-row pitch and total_styles/total_pitch INTO the data schema and JSON. That must be REVERSED: styling and structure belong to each report type's OWN self-contained template/renderer (which reproduces that report type's original PDF faithfully), fed by PURE data. This matches the README's founding principle ('Competency colours are deterministic... never stored'; 'Everything that varies is data; chrome is only the fixed furniture'). So each self-contained per-report template encodes its own faithful styling keyed to the report type, and the JSON stops storing CellStyle/pitch/total_styles/total_pitch. Colours that are genuinely data-derived (e.g. competency band) are computed deterministically by the template from the data label/GPA, never stored as a hex in the data.
authoritative_preference: Two durable, authoritative user preferences drive this task: (A) each report is self-contained - its own structure and its own complete styling, no shared CSS / no shared chrome / no cross-report harmonization; (B) DATA IS DATA NOT STYLES - the extracted data JSON/schema carries only report figures+structure, and the template owns all presentation. Both are hard requirements; the second was added via live steering and REVERSES the prior task's decision to store CellStyle/pitch in the data.
